full_judgment: 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell, can be stated thus, the plaintiff-opposite party filed the original suit being title suit no. 368 of 1984 in the 1st Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka which was transferred to the Additional Court of Munsif and renumbered as Title Suit No. 73 of 1986 for declaration and permanent injunction contending inter alia that the plaintiff is a bonafide business man who purchased the possession of the suit shop from one Md. Selim at a consideration of Tk. 30,000/- (thirty thousand) on 19.12.1979 and since then he is running his business as a shop of cycle and cycle parts. The plaintiff is a member of Mohammadpur Bazar Committee under Dhaka Metropolitan Area and during the continuance of plaintiff's possession a litigation was cropped up between the market committee and the shop-keepers regarding the recognition of the possessors in the shops. Several meetings were held between the market committee and the representative of the shop-keepers in presence of concerned minister in charge and it was decided that a survey team after physical survey would prepare a list of businessman who are found in occupation of the shops. Accordingly, a survey team was constituted and after survey they .submitted a report to the concern ministry of the Government on 16.03.1981 and the plaintiff's name was listed in serial no. 19. Before final publication of the said list a subsequent survey was held on a dispute by a legally constituted survey team and in the said survey report which was published finally in the year 1984 the name of the plaintiff has been enlisted in serial no. 24. On the basis of that final list the defendant no. 1 who is the Administrative officer, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Mohammadpur, Dhaka issued an offer letter in favour of the plaintiff on 07.06.1984 asking the plaintiff to deposit Tk. 30,000/-(thirty thousand) as compensation and arrear rent of the suit shop in 3(three) instalments in order to get allotment of the shop. Accordingly the plaintiff paid Tk. 15,000/-(fifteen thousand) of first installment within the prescribed time on 10.06.1984. But on the same date the plaintiff received a letter showing that his allotment offer was issued on mistake and therefore it was cancelled. Being aggrieved by that letter the plaintiff filed the original suit.
